question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x+5} & ={7}^{6-2x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x+5}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{6-2x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(6-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(6-2x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x & =\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)}\end{aligned}
$$
